drafter.private_reasoning: The existing tracked deletion contains privileged negotiating information. Remove all tracked changes before circulation; do not reproduce the deleted material in comments or the cover note. The draft does not specify an agreed price, so leave an explicit placeholder for partner approval rather than inventing authority to make a price proposal. Narrow the Seller's representations and indemnity and require payment at Closing. Confirm the final export contains no recoverable internal notes before sending.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Counsel, attached is our initial proposed revision. We have clarified payment mechanics, qualified the financial-statement representation, and proposed a defined scope and limitations for Seller indemnification. The purchase price remains open for agreement. Please provide Buyer's proposed closing conditions and any requested disclosure schedules so we can develop a complete signing draft.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares shall be USD [to be agreed before signing] (the “Purchase Price”). At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price to the Seller by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller, against delivery of the Shares, without set-off or counterclaim.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the benefiting party of the closing conditions expressly set forth in this Agreement, on a date mutually agreed in writing. The Buyer's obligation to close shall not be subject to obtaining financing.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as disclosed in the disclosure schedules delivered before signing, the Seller represents that, to the Seller's actual knowledge, the financial statements identified in those schedules fairly present, in all material respects, the Company's financial position and results of operations for the periods covered, in accordance with the accounting principles specified therein, consistently applied, subject, in the case of unaudited statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes.

4. INDEMNITY. Following Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for actual, documented losses directly resulting from a breach of the Seller's express representations or covenants in this Agreement. The Seller shall not be liable for matters disclosed in this Agreement or the disclosure schedules, reflected or reserved for in the financial statements, or actually known to the Buyer before signing. Representation claims must be notified in writing, with reasonable detail, within twelve months after Closing. The Seller's aggregate liability shall not exceed ten percent of the Purchase Price. Recoverable losses shall be reduced by insurance proceeds and other recoveries actually received for the same loss, net of reasonable recovery costs, and shall exclude punitive damages except to the extent payable to a third party. The Buyer shall take reasonable steps to mitigate losses and shall not recover twice for the same loss. This Section shall be the Buyer's exclusive monetary remedy following Closing, except for fraud by the Seller or liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

partner.private_reasoning: The rendered agreement and cover note do not disclose the Seller’s confidential minimum price; the purchase price remains open. Remove non-rendered content before transmission to prevent disclosure through unreviewed annotations, revisions, or embedded information.

receiver.message_back: Buyer proposes a cash-free, debt-free price subject to diligence and a normalized working-capital adjustment, with 15% held in escrow for 24 months; closing conditions must include satisfactory diligence, accuracy of Seller’s representations at Closing, material covenant compliance, required consents and approvals, no injunction or material adverse change, and delivery of unencumbered title to the Shares, supported by pre-signing schedules covering capitalization, financials, debt, taxes, material contracts, litigation, compliance, employees, IP and related-party dealings. Remove the financial-statement knowledge qualifier and the blanket no-set-off restriction; expand customary Seller representations and indemnification, provide 24-month general survival and a 30% general cap with a deductible basket not exceeding 0.5% of price, exclude title, authority, capitalization, taxes, fraud and covenant claims from those general limits, and reject blanket disclosed-matter, reserve and Buyer-knowledge exclusions or exclusive-remedy language that would defeat specific indemnities, equitable relief or purchase-price adjustments.

drafter.private_reasoning: Propose a balanced Seller counter with objective closing conditions, limited escrow and general indemnity exposure, and targeted exceptions. Leave price open pending express agreement. Confidential pricing instructions are not included in the outgoing draft or cover note.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We have revised the draft to accept a cash-free, debt-free structure with a normalized working-capital adjustment, remove the financial-statement knowledge qualifier, expand Seller representations and schedules, and add objective closing conditions. Diligence must be completed before signing rather than remain a discretionary closing condition. As a package, Seller proposes a 5% escrow for 12 months, 18-month general survival, a 15% general cap and a 0.5% deductible basket, with separate treatment for fundamental representations, taxes, covenants and fraud. The revised remedy provisions preserve specific indemnities, equitable relief and price adjustments while preventing double recovery. Price and the accounting and escrow mechanics remain subject to express agreement before signing.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The purchase price for the Shares shall be based on an enterprise value of USD [to be agreed before signing], on a cash-free, debt-free basis, increased by Closing cash, reduced by Closing indebtedness and unpaid Company transaction expenses, and adjusted upward or downward by the amount by which Closing working capital exceeds or falls below an agreed normalized working-capital target (the resulting amount, the “Purchase Price”). The target, definitions, accounting policies and illustrative calculation shall be agreed in a schedule before signing, with no item counted more than once. At Closing, Buyer shall pay the estimated Purchase Price by wire transfer of immediately available funds, with 95% paid to Seller and 5% deposited with an independent escrow agent under an escrow agreement agreed before signing. The escrow shall secure indemnity claims and be released twelve months after Closing, less amounts reasonably reserved for specifically identified, timely notified unresolved claims. Buyer shall deliver its proposed final Closing statement within sixty days after Closing; Seller shall have thirty days to object. Unresolved accounting disputes shall be submitted to an independent accountant acting as expert, whose determination shall be binding absent manifest error. Any resulting payment shall be made within five business days after final determination. Buyer may not withhold Closing payments for disputed indemnity claims. After Closing, set-off is permitted only for amounts agreed in writing or finally adjudicated, subject to this Agreement's applicable limits.
edits.name: Purchase price and adjustment

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing, on a mutually agreed date, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the benefiting party of the express conditions in this Agreement. Buyer shall complete its diligence before signing; neither further diligence nor financing shall be a condition to Closing. Buyer's conditions shall be: Seller's title, authority and capitalization representations being true in all material respects at Closing; Seller's other representations being true at Closing except for inaccuracies that, individually or collectively, would not constitute a Material Adverse Effect, in each case respecting representations expressly made as of a specified date; Seller's material compliance with its pre-Closing covenants; receipt of the consents and regulatory approvals specifically listed before signing in the closing-conditions schedule; absence of an injunction or law prohibiting Closing; absence of a Material Adverse Effect since signing; and delivery of title to the Shares free of liens other than transfer restrictions imposed by securities laws or liens created by Buyer. Seller's conditions shall be Buyer's material compliance with its obligations, accuracy in all material respects of Buyer's authority representations, receipt of the required regulatory approvals, absence of any legal prohibition on Closing, and payment of the amounts required at Closing. “Material Adverse Effect” means a material adverse effect on the Company's business, assets, financial condition or results of operations, taken as a whole, excluding general economic, market or industry conditions, changes in law or accounting principles, war, terrorism, natural disasters and pandemics, except to the extent disproportionately affecting the Company relative to comparable businesses, and excluding effects of the announcement of this transaction or actions required by this Agreement.
edits.name: Objective closing conditions

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the exception in the disclosure schedules delivered before signing, Seller represents that: (a) Seller has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and owns the Shares free of liens other than applicable securities-law transfer restrictions; (b) the Company is duly organized, validly existing and has authority to conduct its business; (c) the capitalization schedule accurately states all outstanding equity interests and rights to acquire equity interests, and the Shares are validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable; (d) the scheduled financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the Company's financial position and results of operations in accordance with the specified accounting principles, consistently applied, subject for unaudited statements to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes; (e) the debt schedule identifies all outstanding indebtedness, and the Company has no material liabilities required to be reflected under those accounting principles other than liabilities reflected or reserved in those statements or incurred in the ordinary course since their date; (f) all material tax returns have been timely filed and are accurate in all material respects, all material taxes due have been paid, and no material tax dispute is pending or, to Seller's actual knowledge, threatened in writing; (g) the material contracts schedule is complete, such contracts are in force, and neither the Company nor, to Seller's actual knowledge, any counterparty is in material default; (h) no material litigation is pending or, to Seller's actual knowledge, threatened in writing; (i) the Company complies in all material respects with applicable laws and holds all material permits; (j) the employee and benefit schedules identify material employment and benefit arrangements, and the Company complies in all material respects with applicable employment laws; (k) the Company owns or has valid rights to use the intellectual property material to its business and, to Seller's actual knowledge, its current operations do not materially infringe third-party intellectual property rights; and (l) the related-party schedule identifies all material related-party transactions and balances. The disclosure schedules shall cover capitalization, financial statements, indebtedness, taxes, material contracts, litigation, compliance, employees and benefits, intellectual property and related-party dealings. A disclosure qualifies another representation only where its relevance is reasonably apparent on its face.
edits.name: Expanded Seller representations

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. Following Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for actual, documented losses resulting from breaches of Seller's express representations or covenants, Company taxes attributable to periods ending on or before Closing and the pre-Closing portion of straddle periods, and any specific indemnities expressly agreed before signing. General representation claims must be notified with reasonable detail within eighteen months after Closing, are subject to a deductible basket equal to 0.5% of the Purchase Price, and are capped in the aggregate at 15% of the Purchase Price. Claims concerning title to the Shares, Seller's authority and capitalization shall survive for six years and shall not be subject to the general basket or cap. Tax claims shall survive until sixty days after expiration of the applicable statutory limitation period and shall not be subject to the general basket or cap. Covenant claims shall not be subject to the general basket or cap; pre-Closing covenant claims must be notified within eighteen months after Closing, and post-Closing covenants survive in accordance with their terms. Specific indemnities shall be governed by their expressly agreed limits and survival periods. Seller's aggregate liability for all claims shall not exceed the Purchase Price, except for Seller's fraud or liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Seller's fraud shall not be subject to the contractual basket, cap or survival periods. Timely notified claims survive until resolved. Fair disclosure qualifies representations only as provided in Section 3 and does not independently exclude liability under covenants or specific indemnities. Neither a financial-statement reserve nor Buyer's knowledge independently bars a claim; recovery is excluded only to the extent the same loss has actually been accounted for through a reduction of the Purchase Price or otherwise recovered. Recoverable losses shall be reduced by insurance proceeds and other third-party recoveries actually received for the same loss, net of reasonable recovery costs, and shall exclude punitive damages except to the extent payable to a third party. Buyer shall take reasonable steps to mitigate losses and shall not recover twice for the same loss. Buyer shall first seek payment from available escrow funds, without delaying recovery otherwise due or making escrow the sole source of recovery. This Section is the exclusive post-Closing monetary remedy for breaches of this Agreement, but does not limit purchase-price adjustments, expressly agreed specific indemnities, equitable relief, Seller's fraud or liability that cannot lawfully be limited.
edits.name: Indemnity compromise

receiver.message_back: Buyer accepts the cash-free, debt-free structure and pre-signing diligence, but counters with a 10% escrow held for 24 months, 24-month general survival, a 20% general cap and a 0.25% tipping basket, preserving the separate protections for fundamental representations, taxes, covenants and fraud and adding a materiality scrape for indemnity breach and loss determinations. Signing remains subject to agreement on price, accounting and escrow mechanics, completed schedules and diligence-driven specific indemnities; fundamental representations must be accurate in all respects at Closing, other representations in all material respects rather than subject to an MAE threshold, with ordinary-course operating covenants and an express termination right if conditions remain unsatisfied at an agreed outside date.
